questions.text:
A company specializes in providing personalized product recommendations for e-commerce platforms. You've been tasked with developing a solution that can quickly generate high-quality product descriptions, tailor marketing copy based on customer preferences, and analyze customer reviews to identify trends in sentiment. Given the scale of data and the need for flexibility in choosing foundational models, you decide to use an AI service that can integrate seamlessly with your existing AWS infrastructure while also offering managed foundational models from third-party providers.

Which AWS service would best meet your requirements?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service offering access to pre-trained foundational models from Amazon and third-party providers (AI21 Labs, Anthropic, Stability AI, etc.), ideal for generating text, marketing copy, and sentiment analysis without managing infrastructure.

options.text: Amazon Rekognition
Amazon SageMaker
Amazon Bedrock
Amazon Personalize

questions.text:
You are tasked with building a predictive model for customer lifetime value (CLV) using Amazon SageMaker. You decide to use SageMaker's automatic model tuning (hyperparameter optimization) with Random Search strategy to fine-tune the model. During the tuning process, you observe that some of the trials are not converging effectively, and the results are not as expected. You suspect that the hyperparameter ranges or the strategy you are using may need adjustment.

Which of the following approaches is MOST LIKELY to improve the effectiveness of the hyperparameter tuning process?
questions.explanation: Bayesian Optimization is more efficient than Random Search for complex models, learning from previous trials to predict the best hyperparameters. Combined with narrowing the range of critical hyperparameters, this improves convergence.

options.text: Switch from the Random Search strategy to the Bayesian Optimization strategy and narrow the range of critical hyperparameters
Increase the number of hyperparameters being tuned and widen the range for all hyperparameters
Decrease the number of total trials but increase the number of parallel jobs to speed up the tuning process
Use the Grid Search strategy with a wide range for all hyperparameters and increase the number of total trials

questions.text:
You are working as a machine learning engineer for a startup that provides image recognition services. The company expects varying levels of traffic, with some days having very few requests and other days experiencing sudden spikes. The company wants to minimize costs during low-traffic periods while still being able to handle large, infrequent spikes of requests efficiently, using Amazon SageMaker for deployment.

Which of the following statements is the BEST recommendation for the given scenario?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference automatically scales compute resources based on incoming requests, so you only pay for compute time used, making it ideal for unpredictable, intermittent traffic with idle periods.

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference
Use Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference
Use Amazon SageMaker Real-time Inference
Use Batch transform to run inference with Amazon SageMaker

questions.text:
You are working on a machine learning project for a financial services company, developing a model to predict credit risk. After deploying the initial version of the model using Amazon SageMaker, you find that its performance, measured by the AUC (Area Under the Curve), is not meeting the company's accuracy requirements. Given limited time and computational resources, you need to prioritize the most impactful strategies.

Which of the following approaches are the MOST LIKELY to lead to a significant improvement in model performance? (Select two)
questions.explanation: Feature engineering with SageMaker Clarify to evaluate feature importance gives the model better signals to learn from. SageMaker Debugger helps identify and fix underlying training problems like overfitting, saturated activations, and vanishing gradients, both of which drive real performance gains.

options.text: Increase the size of the training dataset by incorporating synthetic data and then retrain the existing model
Switch to a more complex algorithm, such as deep learning, and use transfer learning to leverage pre-trained models
Focus on feature engineering by creating domain-specific features and use SageMaker Clarify to evaluate feature importance
Use Amazon SageMaker Debugger to debug and improve model performance by addressing underlying problems such as overfitting, saturated activation functions, and vanishing gradients
Perform hyperparameter tuning using Bayesian optimization and increase the number of trials to explore a broader search space

questions.text:
You are a machine learning engineer working for a telecommunications company that needs to develop a predictive maintenance model to predict when network equipment is likely to fail based on historical sensor data, avoiding unplanned downtime and optimizing maintenance schedules.

Given the nature of the data and the business objective, which Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithm is the MOST SUITABLE for this use case?
questions.explanation: Random Cut Forest (RCF) is an unsupervised algorithm specifically designed to detect anomalous data points, making it ideal for spotting the unusual sensor patterns that precede equipment failure in near real-time.

options.text: DeepAR Algorithm to forecast future equipment failures based on historical data
Linear Learner Algorithm to classify equipment status as 'healthy' or 'at risk' based on sensor readings
Random Cut Forest (RCF) Algorithm to detect anomalies in sensor data that may indicate impending failures
Time Series K-Means Algorithm to cluster similar patterns in the sensor data and predict failures

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at a financial technology company developing a fraud detection system on a large, highly imbalanced dataset where only a small percentage of transactions are labeled fraudulent. Your team has access to Amazon SageMaker and is considering various built-in algorithms to build the model.

Given the need for both high accuracy and the ability to handle imbalanced data, which SageMaker built-in algorithm is the MOST SUITABLE for this use case?
questions.explanation: XGBoost handles imbalanced, structured data extremely well, supporting custom objective functions and built-in techniques (like scale_pos_weight) to optimize for precision and recall on the minority class.

options.text: Use the Linear Learner algorithm with weighted classification to address the class imbalance
Apply the XGBoost algorithm with a custom objective function to optimize for precision and recall
Select the Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm for its ability to detect anomalies in transaction data
Implement the K-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) algorithm to classify transactions based on similarity to known fraudulent cases

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at a healthcare startup tasked with developing a machine learning model to predict the likelihood of patients developing a specific chronic disease. The dataset available includes patient demographics, medical history, lab results, and lifestyle factors, but it is relatively small (1,000 records), has missing values in critical features, and the class distribution is highly imbalanced (only 5% positive).

Given the data limitations, which of the following approaches is the MOST LIKELY to determine the feasibility of an ML solution and guide your next steps?
questions.explanation: Conducting exploratory data analysis (EDA) first lets you understand data distribution, address missing values, and assess class imbalance before deciding whether an ML solution is feasible and what preprocessing is needed.

options.text: Proceed with training a deep neural network (DNN) model using the available data, as DNNs can handle small datasets by learning complex patterns
Increase the dataset size by generating synthetic data and then train a simple logistic regression model to avoid overfitting
Conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA) to understand the data distribution, address missing values, and assess the class imbalance before determining if an ML solution is feasible
Immediately apply an oversampling technique to balance the dataset, then train an XGBoost model to maximize performance on the minority class

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at a marketing agency tasked with creating a sentiment analysis model to analyze customer reviews. The company wants to quickly deploy a solution with minimal training time and development effort, leveraging a pre-trained natural language processing (NLP) model fine-tuned with a custom dataset of labeled customer reviews. Your team has access to both Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker JumpStart.

Which approach is the MOST APPROPRIATE for fine-tuning the pre-trained model with your custom dataset?
questions.explanation: SageMaker JumpStart lets you deploy a pre-trained NLP model and use its built-in fine-tuning functionality directly with a custom dataset, minimizing development time and infrastructure management.

options.text: Use Amazon Bedrock to select a base foundation model from a third-party provider, then fine-tune the base model directly in the Bedrock interface using your custom dataset
Use SageMaker JumpStart to deploy a pre-trained NLP model and use the built-in fine-tuning functionality with your custom dataset to create a customized sentiment analysis model
Use Amazon Bedrock to train a model from scratch using your custom dataset, as Bedrock is optimized for training large models efficiently
Use SageMaker JumpStart to create a custom container for your pre-trained model and manually implement fine-tuning with TensorFlow

questions.text:
You are working as a data scientist at a financial services company tasked with developing a credit risk prediction model. After experimenting with logistic regression, decision trees, and support vector machines, none of the models individually achieves the desired accuracy and robustness. Your goal is to improve overall performance by combining these models to leverage their strengths while minimizing weaknesses.

Which of the following approaches is the MOST LIKELY to improve the model's performance?
questions.explanation: Stacking trains a meta-model (e.g. random forest) on the predictions of the base models, letting the meta-model learn to leverage each base model's strengths while compensating for their weaknesses.

options.text: Use a simple voting ensemble, where the final prediction is based on the majority vote from the logistic regression, decision tree, and support vector machine models
Implement boosting by training sequentially different types of models, where each new model corrects the errors of the previous ones
Apply stacking, where the predictions from logistic regression, decision trees, and support vector machines are used as inputs to a meta-model, such as a random forest, to make the final prediction
Use bagging, where different types of models are trained on different subsets of the data, and their predictions are averaged to produce the final result

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at a financial institution tasked with building a model to detect fraudulent transactions on a highly imbalanced dataset. You decide to implement a boosting technique, considering AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost.

Given the problem context and the need to effectively handle class imbalance, which boosting technique is MOST SUITABLE for this scenario?
questions.explanation: XGBoost extends Gradient Boosting with regularization, handling of missing values, and support for weighted classes, plus significant computational efficiency, making it well suited for imbalanced fraud data.

options.text: Use Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost) to focus on correcting the errors of weak classifiers, giving more weight to incorrectly classified instances during each iteration
Apply Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for its ability to handle imbalanced datasets effectively through regularization, weighted classes, and optimized computational efficiency
Implement Gradient Boosting to sequentially train weak learners, using the gradient of the loss function to improve performance on the minority class
Use Gradient Boosting and manually adjust the learning rate and class weights to improve performance on the minority class, avoiding the complexities of XGBoost

questions.text:
You are a data scientist working on a deep learning model to classify medical images for disease detection. The model shows high accuracy on training data but performs poorly on the validation set, indicating overfitting. The dataset is limited in size, and the model is complex with many parameters.

Which combination of techniques is the MOST LIKELY to help prevent overfitting and improve the model's performance on unseen data?
questions.explanation: Data augmentation expands the effective size and diversity of a limited training set, early stopping halts training before the model overtrains, and ensembling averages predictions across multiple models to reduce the impact of any single model's overfitting.

options.text: Apply early stopping to halt training when the validation loss stops improving, and use dropout as a regularization technique to prevent the model from becoming too reliant on specific neurons
Use ensembling by combining multiple versions of the same model trained with different random seeds, and apply data augmentation to artificially increase the size of the dataset
Prune the model by removing less important layers and nodes, and use L2 regularization to reduce the magnitude of the model's weights, preventing overfitting
Combine data augmentation to increase the diversity of the training data with early stopping to prevent overfitting, and use ensembling to average predictions from multiple models

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at a pharmaceutical company that builds predictive models to analyze clinical trial data. Due to regulatory requirements, the company must maintain strict version control of all models used in decision-making, tracking data, hyperparameters, and code, and ensuring models can be reproduced and audited in the future.

Which of the following strategies is the MOST LIKELY to ensure model versioning, repeatability, and auditability?
questions.explanation: The SageMaker Model Registry is purpose-built to register, track, and manage model versions along with metadata like data sources, hyperparameters, and training code, providing automated versioning and audit trails.

options.text: Use Amazon S3 to store each version of the model manually, tagging the stored files with metadata about the training data, hyperparameters, and code used for training
Leverage the SageMaker Model Registry to register, track, and manage different versions of models, capturing all relevant metadata, including data sources, hyperparameters, and training code
Create a version control system in Git for the model's training code and configuration files, while storing the trained models in a separate S3 bucket for easy retrieval
Use SageMaker Model Monitor to track the performance of models in production, ensuring that any changes in model behavior are documented for future audits

questions.text:
You are a Data Scientist working for an e-commerce company developing a machine learning model to predict whether a customer will make a purchase based on browsing behavior. The dataset is imbalanced, with a small percentage of customers making a purchase.

Which of the following evaluation techniques and metrics should you prioritize when assessing the performance of your model, considering the dataset's imbalance and the need for a comprehensive understanding of both false positives and false negatives? (Select two)
questions.explanation: The confusion matrix reveals true/false positives and negatives directly, and precision/recall focus specifically on the model's ability to correctly identify the positive (minority) class while accounting for both false positives and false negatives — far more informative than accuracy on an imbalanced dataset.

options.text: Evaluate the model using the confusion matrix, which provides insights into true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives, allowing you to calculate additional metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 score
Use accuracy as the primary metric, as it measures the percentage of correct predictions out of all predictions made by the model
Prioritize Root mean squared error (RMSE) as the key metric, as it measures the average magnitude of the errors between predicted and actual values
Utilize the AUC-ROC curve to evaluate the model's ability to distinguish between classes across various thresholds, particularly in the presence of class imbalance
Use precision and recall to focus on the model's ability to correctly identify positive cases while minimizing false positives and false negatives

questions.text:
You are a data scientist working on a binary classification model to predict whether customers will default on their loans. The dataset is highly imbalanced, with only 10% of customers having defaulted. You decide to use the ROC curve and AUC to evaluate the model.

Which of the following interpretations of the ROC and AUC metrics is MOST ACCURATE for assessing the model's performance?
questions.explanation: An AUC close to 1.0 means the model has excellent discriminatory power across all thresholds, effectively separating defaulters from non-defaulters, independent of class imbalance.

options.text: A ROC curve that is close to the diagonal line (AUC ~ 0.5) indicates that the model performs well across all thresholds
An AUC close to 1.0 indicates that the model has excellent discriminatory power, effectively distinguishing between defaulters and non-defaulters
A ROC curve that is closer to the top-left corner of the plot (AUC ~ 1) shows that the model is overfitting, and its predictions are too optimistic
An AUC close to 0 indicates that the model is highly accurate, correctly classifying almost all instances of defaulters and non-defaulters

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at an insurance company developing a model to predict fraudulent claims, with a strong commitment to fairness so the model doesn't disproportionately affect any demographic group. You use Amazon SageMaker Clarify's Conditional Demographic Disparity (CDD) to understand how the model's predictions differ across demographic groups when conditioned on a relevant factor like income.

Which of the following BEST describes how CDD can be used to assess and mitigate bias in your model?
questions.explanation: CDD measures the difference in positive prediction rates across demographic groups while conditioning on a relevant feature like income, revealing subtler bias that a simple overall comparison would mask.

options.text: CDD measures the difference in average predicted outcomes between demographic groups, helping to identify overall bias without considering other factors
CDD assesses the proportion of correctly predicted outcomes for each demographic group, helping to ensure that the model is equally accurate across groups

CDD evaluates the disparity in positive prediction rates across demographic groups, conditioned on a specific feature like income, to detect bias that may not be apparent when only considering overall outcomes
CDD focuses on the relationship between feature importance and demographic groups, highlighting whether certain features disproportionately influence predictions for specific groups

questions.text:
You are a machine learning engineer at a financial services company tasked with building a real-time fraud detection system. The company has a limited budget for cloud resources, and the model needs to be retrained frequently to adapt to new fraud patterns. You must carefully balance model performance, training time, and cost.

Which of the following strategies is the MOST LIKELY to achieve an optimal balance between model performance, training time, and cost?
questions.explanation: XGBoost with early stopping and hyperparameter tuning delivers strong accuracy while keeping training time and computational cost efficient, striking a better balance than deep neural networks, plain logistic regression, or nonlinear SVMs for this use case.

options.text: Use a deep neural network with multiple layers and complex architecture to maximize performance, even if it requires significant computational resources and longer training times
Deploy a simpler model like logistic regression to reduce training time and cost, while accepting a slight reduction in model accuracy
Implement a tree-based model like XGBoost with early stopping and hyperparameter tuning, balancing accuracy with reduced training time and computational cost
Choose a support vector machine (SVM) with a nonlinear kernel to enhance accuracy, regardless of the increased training time and cost associated with large datasets

questions.text:
You are an ML Engineer working for a healthcare company that uses a machine learning model on Amazon SageMaker to recommend personalized treatment plans to patients. A new version of the model has been developed, and you need to deploy it in production while being able to quickly roll back to the previous version if any issues arise, maintaining version control and managing traffic between versions.

Which of the following strategies should you implement to ensure a smooth and reliable deployment, considering best practices for versioning and rollback? (Select two)
questions.explanation: SageMaker's built-in model versioning combined with a canary release limits exposure by routing a small percentage of traffic to the new model first; a blue/green deployment strategy lets you gradually shift traffic and monitor performance, with automatic rollback if CloudWatch alarms trip.

options.text: Deploy the new model version immediately and redirect 100% of traffic to it, assuming it has been thoroughly tested and will not require a rollback
Create a backup of the current model, deploy the new version, and if any issues arise, manually roll back by redeploying the previous model version
Deploy the new model version alongside the current one, and use Amazon SageMaker's multi-model endpoint to serve both models simultaneously, splitting traffic between them
Use Amazon SageMaker's built-in versioning to manage different versions of the model, and deploy the new version in a canary release by redirecting a small percentage of traffic to it initially
Utilize Amazon SageMaker's blue/green deployment strategy to shift traffic gradually from the old model to the new one, ensuring that you can monitor performance and quickly revert if needed

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at a healthcare company developing a machine learning model to analyze medical imaging data (X-rays, MRIs). The dataset consists of 10 million high-resolution images stored in Amazon S3, amounting to several terabytes. Training must process these images efficiently to avoid I/O bottlenecks.

Given the size and nature of the dataset, which SageMaker input mode is the MOST SUITABLE for this use case?
questions.explanation: Pipe input mode streams data directly from Amazon S3 into the training instances at high throughput, letting training start immediately without needing to store the entire dataset locally first — ideal for very large datasets.

options.text: Use the File input mode to download the entire dataset from Amazon S3 to the training instances' local storage before starting the training process, ensuring that all data is available locally during training

Select the Pipe input mode to stream the data directly from Amazon S3 to the training instances, allowing the model to start processing data immediately without requiring local storage for the entire dataset
Implement the FastFile input mode with FSx for Lustre, to enable on-demand streaming of data chunks from Amazon S3 with low latency and high throughput
Use the File input mode with EFS (Amazon Elastic File System) to mount the dataset across multiple instances, ensuring data is shared and accessible during distributed training

questions.text:
You are a machine learning engineer at a healthcare company responsible for developing and deploying an end-to-end ML workflow for predicting patient readmission rates, involving data preprocessing, model training, hyperparameter tuning, and deployment, with support for regular retraining as new data becomes available and minimal manual intervention.

Given these requirements, which of the following options is the MOST SUITABLE for orchestrating your ML workflow?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Pipelines is purpose-built to orchestrate end-to-end ML workflows, integrating data processing, training, tuning, and deployment with built-in versioning, lineage tracking, and CI/CD support.

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions to define and orchestrate each step of the ML workflow, integrate with SageMaker for model training and deployment, and leverage AWS Lambda for data preprocessing tasks
Leverage Amazon EC2 instances to manually execute each step of the ML workflow, use Amazon RDS for storing intermediate results, and deploy the model using Amazon SageMaker endpoints
Implement the entire ML workflow using Amazon SageMaker Pipelines, which provides integrated orchestration for data processing, model training, tuning, and deployment
Use AWS Glue for data preprocessing, Amazon SageMaker for model training and tuning, and manually deploy the model to an Amazon EC2 instance for inference

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at a retail company responsible for deploying a machine learning model that predicts customer purchase behavior. The model needs to serve real-time, low-latency predictions for a recommendation engine and must scale to handle varying traffic loads during peak shopping periods like Black Friday, with monitoring and automatic rollout of updates.

Given these requirements, which AWS deployment service and configuration is the MOST SUITABLE for deploying the machine learning model?
questions.explanation: SageMaker real-time hosting with an auto-scaling endpoint automatically adjusts instance count based on traffic demand, ensuring low latency and scalability during peak periods, plus built-in monitoring and versioning.

options.text: Deploy the model using Amazon SageMaker real-time hosting services with an auto-scaling endpoint, enabling you to automatically adjust the number of instances based on traffic demand
Deploy the model on Amazon EC2 instances with a load balancer to distribute traffic, manually scaling the instances based on expected traffic during peak periods
Use AWS Lambda to deploy the model as a serverless function, automatically scaling based on the number of requests, and store the model artifacts in Amazon S3
Deploy the model on Amazon SageMaker with batch transform jobs, running the jobs periodically to generate predictions and storing the results in Amazon S3 for the recommendation engine

questions.text:
You are an ML Engineer working for a logistics company that uses multiple machine learning models to optimize delivery routes in real-time, needing to balance performance, cost, and latency, with strict cost constraints and slight variations in model access frequency.

Which of the following strategies should you consider to balance the tradeoffs between performance, cost, and latency when deploying your model in Amazon SageMaker? (Select two)
questions.explanation: A multi-model endpoint shares resources across models to reduce cost, and auto-scaling on a fleet of medium instances dynamically adjusts capacity to demand — together balancing cost, performance, and latency better than fixed high-end or fixed low-end instance choices.

options.text: Deploy the model on a high-performance GPU instance to minimize latency, regardless of the higher cost, ensuring real-time route adjustments
Choose a lower-cost CPU instance, accepting longer inference times, as the savings on compute costs are more important than minimizing latency
Use Amazon SageMaker's multi-model endpoint to deploy multiple models on a single instance, reducing costs by sharing resources
Implement auto-scaling on a fleet of medium-sized instances, allowing the system to adjust resources based on real-time demand, balancing cost and performance dynamically
Leverage Amazon SageMaker Neo to compile the model for optimized deployment on edge devices, reducing latency and cost but with limited scalability for large datasets

questions.text:
You are a machine learning engineer at a fintech company tasked with developing and deploying an end-to-end machine learning workflow for fraud detection, involving data extraction, preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, hyperparameter tuning, and deployment. The solution must be scalable, support complex task dependencies, provide robust monitoring/versioning, and integrate with AWS services.

Which deployment orchestrator is the MOST SUITABLE for managing and automating your ML workflow?
questions.explanation: SageMaker Pipelines is purpose-built for ML workflow orchestration, with native integration for training, tuning, and deployment, plus built-in versioning and lineage tracking — a better fit than general-purpose tools like Airflow, Step Functions, or manual Lambda triggers.

options.text: Use Apache Airflow to define and manage the workflow with custom DAGs, integrating with AWS services through operators and hooks
Use Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to orchestrate the entire ML workflow, leveraging its built-in integration with SageMaker features like training, tuning, and deployment
Use AWS Step Functions to build a serverless workflow that integrates with SageMaker for model training and deployment, ensuring scalability and fault tolerance
Use AWS Lambda functions to manually trigger each step of the ML workflow, enabling flexible execution without needing a predefined orchestration tool

questions.text:
You are a Machine Learning Engineer at a large retail company with models for personalized recommendations (real-time, low latency), generative AI (high scalability for fluctuating loads), and fraud detection (large model needing serverless integration to minimize infrastructure management).

Which of the following deployment targets should you choose for the different machine learning models, given their specific requirements? (Select two)
questions.explanation: SageMaker endpoints provide fully managed, low-latency real-time inference ideal for the recommendation model, while Amazon EKS offers the containerized orchestration and scalability needed for the generative AI model's fluctuating demand.

options.text: Use AWS Lambda to deploy the fraud detection model, which requires rapid scaling and integration into an existing serverless architecture, minimizing infrastructure management

Choose Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) for the recommendation model, as it provides container orchestration for large-scale, batch processing workloads with tight integration into other AWS services
Deploy all models using Amazon SageMaker endpoints for consistency and ease of management, regardless of their individual requirements for scalability, latency, or integration
Deploy the real-time recommendation model using Amazon SageMaker endpoints to ensure low-latency, high-availability, and managed infrastructure for real-time inference
Deploy the generative AI model using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to leverage containerized microservices for high scalability and control over the deployment environment

questions.text:
You are an ML engineer at a startup developing a recommendation engine. Training jobs are sporadic but require significant computational power, while inference workloads must handle varying traffic throughout the day. The company is cost-conscious and aims to balance cost efficiency with scalability and performance.

Given these requirements, which approach to resource allocation is the MOST SUITABLE for training and inference, and why?
questions.explanation: On-demand instances give training the flexibility to scale only when sporadic jobs run, while provisioned resources with auto-scaling let inference handle varying traffic efficiently while controlling costs during low-demand periods.

options.text: Use on-demand instances for both training and inference to ensure that the company only pays for the compute resources it uses when it needs them, avoiding any upfront commitments
Use provisioned resources with reserved instances for both training and inference to lock in lower costs and guarantee resource availability, ensuring predictability in budgeting

Use on-demand instances for training, allowing the flexibility to scale resources as needed, and use provisioned resources with auto-scaling for inference to handle varying traffic while controlling costs
Use provisioned resources with spot instances for both training and inference to take advantage of the lowest possible costs, accepting the potential for interruptions during workload execution

questions.text:
You are an ML engineer at a retail company that uses a SageMaker model to generate product recommendations in real-time. During peak shopping periods, traffic increases dramatically, and you need the endpoint to handle spikes without compromising response time, while optimizing costs during low demand.

Which scaling policy is the MOST SUITABLE for this scenario, and why?
questions.explanation: A target tracking scaling policy continuously adjusts instance count to maintain a predefined metric (e.g. invocations per instance), responding smoothly to unpredictable traffic spikes while scaling down during quiet periods.

options.text: Use a target tracking scaling policy that automatically adjusts the number of instances based on a predefined target metric, such as CPU utilization or invocations per instance, to maintain a steady level of performance during traffic spikes
Use a step scaling policy that adjusts the number of instances based on the size of the traffic spike, adding a set number of instances for each level of increased demand

Use scheduled scaling to preemptively add or remove instances based on anticipated traffic patterns, such as known peak times during Black Friday, to ensure sufficient capacity is available when needed
Use a manual scaling policy where you adjust the number of instances based on real-time monitoring of traffic, allowing you to fine-tune resource allocation as needed during high-demand periods

questions.text:
You are a lead machine learning engineer at a growing tech startup developing a recommendation system for a mobile app. The engine must scale quickly, remain cost-effective, and be easy to maintain by a small team, using AWS for ML infrastructure.

Which combination of practices and AWS services is MOST LIKELY to result in a maintainable, scalable, and cost-effective ML infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Using SageMaker for both training and deployment with auto-scaling endpoints reduces operational overhead, and SageMaker Pipelines automates the entire workflow end-to-end, giving scalability and maintainability with minimal manual effort.

options.text: Implement Amazon SageMaker for model training, deploy the models using Amazon EC2 with manual scaling to handle inference, and use AWS CloudFormation for managing infrastructure as code to ensure repeatability

Use Amazon SageMaker for both training and deployment, leverage auto-scaling endpoints for real-time inference, and apply SageMaker Pipelines for orchestrating end-to-end ML workflows, ensuring scalability and automation
Train models using Amazon EMR for cost efficiency, deploy the models using AWS Lambda for serverless inference, and manually monitor the system using CloudWatch to reduce operational overhead

Use Amazon SageMaker for training, deploy models on Amazon ECS for flexible scaling, and implement infrastructure monitoring with a combination of CloudWatch and AWS Systems Manager to ensure maintainability

questions.text:
You are an ML engineer at a data analytics company training a deep learning model on a large, computationally intensive dataset. The training job can tolerate interruptions and may run for hours or days, and the company has a limited budget for cloud infrastructure.

Which strategy is the MOST EFFECTIVE for your ML training job while minimizing cost and ensuring the job completes successfully?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Managed Spot Training dynamically allocates Spot Instances and automatically resumes interrupted jobs from checkpoints, providing the best combination of automation and cost savings for an interruption-tolerant training job.

options.text: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to automatically add Spot Instances to the training job based on demand, and configure the job to continue processing even if some Spot Instances are interrupted
Deploy the training job on a fixed number of On-Demand EC2 instances to ensure stability, and manually add Spot Instances as needed to speed up the job during off-peak hours
Use Amazon SageMaker Managed Spot Training to dynamically allocate Spot Instances for the training job, automatically retrying any interrupted instances via checkpoints
Start the training job using only Spot Instances to minimize cost, and switch to On-Demand instances manually if any Spot Instances are interrupted during training

questions.text:
You are an ML engineer at an e-commerce company building an automated recommendation system that scales during peak shopping seasons. The solution requires provisioning SageMaker, EC2, and RDS resources, automating deployment and management, and ensuring stacks communicate effectively, prioritizing infrastructure as code (IaC).

Which approach is the MOST SUITABLE for automating the provisioning of compute resources and ensuring seamless communication between stacks?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation with nested stacks modularizes infrastructure, and passing outputs from one stack as inputs to another automates provisioning while ensuring reliable, consistent communication between the SageMaker, EC2, and RDS resources.

options.text: Use AWS CloudFormation with nested stacks to automate the provisioning of SageMaker, EC2, and RDS resources, and configure outputs from one stack as inputs to another to enable communication between them
Use AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit) to define the infrastructure in a high-level programming language, deploying each service as an independent stack without configuring inter-stack communication

Manually provision the SageMaker, EC2, and RDS resources using the AWS Management Console, ensuring that communication is established by manually updating security groups and networking configurations
Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy the entire ML solution, relying on its built-in environment management to handle the provisioning and communication between resources automatically

questions.text:
You are a machine learning engineer at a biotech company developing a custom deep learning model for genomic data analysis, using a specific TensorFlow version with custom Python libraries not available in standard SageMaker environments. You decide to use the 'Bring Your Own Container' (BYOC) approach.

Which steps are MOST IMPORTANT for successfully deploying your custom container with SageMaker, ensuring it meets the company's requirements?
questions.explanation: Building a Docker container with the required environment, pushing it to Amazon ECR, and using SageMaker's Script Mode to run your training script inside the container is the standard, integrated approach to BYOC on SageMaker.

options.text: Build a Docker container with the required TensorFlow version and dependencies, push the container image to Docker Hub, and reference the image in SageMaker when creating the training job

Create a Docker container with the required environment, push the container image to Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry), and use SageMaker's Script Mode to execute the training script within the container

questions.text:

questions.explanation: Continuous monitoring of input features and predictions with statistical tests detects distribution shifts early, and periodically retraining on recent data (with versioning to track improvements) keeps the model aligned with current real-world patterns.

options.text: Deploy a secondary model trained on different data and compare its predictions with the original model to detect any significant differences, indicating potential drift

Retrain the model on the most recent data to ensure it captures current trends, and use model versioning to track performance improvements over time
Decrease the complexity of the model by removing features and layers, thereby turning it into a simpler model that can handle various types of data distributions

SageMaker Model Monitor tracks input data distribution changes to catch data drift, while periodic retraining on updated data addresses model drift.

options.text: Data drift occurs when the distribution of the input data changes over time, while model drift happens when the model's underlying assumptions or parameters become outdated. Data drift refers to changes in the model's accuracy due to shifts in the data, while model drift refers to changes in the underlying data features over time. To address both, you should use SageMaker Clarify to detect bias and retrain the model monthly

Data drift occurs when the model's predictions start to deviate from the expected outcomes, while model drift occurs when the model's accuracy declines due to changes in the input data. SageMaker Pipelines should be used to automate retraining for both types of drift

Data drift is a sudden change in the model's accuracy, while model drift is a gradual degradation in model performance. You should use SageMaker Feature Store to manage both types of drift by standardizing input data

questions.text:
You are a data scientist at a credit risk management company. To ensure transparency and regulatory compliance, you need to explain how the model makes its predictions — a detailed understanding of individual features' influence for specific customers, as well as an overall view of feature impact across the entire dataset.

Which of the following explanations BEST describes the differences between Shapley values and Partial Dependence Plots (PDP) in the context of model explainability, and how you might use them for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Shapley values are a local method that quantifies each feature's contribution to a specific prediction; PDP is a global method showing the marginal effect of a feature on predictions across the whole dataset. Use Shapley values for individual explanations, PDP for dataset-level trends.

options.text: Shapley values provide a global view of the model's behavior by measuring the average effect of each feature across all instances, while PDP offers a local view by showing the effect of a single feature on the model's prediction for a specific instance. Use Shapley values to understand overall feature importance and PDP to interpret individual predictions

Shapley values provide a local explanation by quantifying the contribution of each feature to the prediction for a specific instance, while PDP provides a global explanation by showing the marginal effect of a feature on the model's predictions across the dataset. Use Shapley values to explain individual predictions and PDP to understand the model's behavior at a dataset level

Shapley values and PDP are both global explainability methods that show the average effect of features on model predictions. Use either method to understand overall feature importance, but Shapley values are computationally less expensive than PDP

Shapley values provide a visual interpretation of feature importance using plots, while PDP provides numeric values indicating the marginal contribution of features to the model's predictions. Use Shapley values for visual analysis and PDP for quantitative analysis

A healthcare company training a neural network to classify medical images observes the model's validation performance improves significantly early on, then begins to degrade after a certain number of epochs.

Which solutions will mitigate this problem? (Select two)
questions.explanation: Early stopping halts training once validation loss stops improving, preventing overfitting; dropout layers randomly deactivate neurons during training, discouraging over-reliance on specific neurons and improving generalization.

options.text: Increase the number of epochs to ensure the model learns the training data thoroughly before stopping
Reduce the size of the training dataset to simplify the learning process and avoid overfitting
Increase the number of layers as well as the number of neurons to prevent overfitting
Use early stopping to halt training once the validation loss stops improving
Add dropout layers to the neural network architecture to prevent overfitting
